events.title: Offerings of the Twelve Tribal Leaders
events.description: On the day Moses finishes setting up the tabernacle, the leaders of the twelve tribes bring wagons and oxen, and present identical dedication offerings for the altar, one leader on each of twelve days.

events.title: The Lampstand and the Dedication of the Levites
events.description: Aaron sets up the seven lamps to give light in front of the lampstand, and the Levites are cleansed, presented as an elevation offering, and given to Aaron in place of the firstborn of Israel.

events.title: The Passover Kept in the Wilderness of Sinai
events.description: Israel keeps the passover in the first month of the second year after leaving Egypt. For those unclean or on a journey, a second passover is appointed in the second month on the fourteenth day.

events.title: The First Census of Israel
events.description: On the first day of the second month of the second year, the LORD commands a census of all Israelite men twenty years and older able to go to war; the total is 603,550.

events.title: The Levites Set Apart for the Tabernacle
events.description: The Levites are not enrolled with the other tribes but appointed over the tabernacle of the covenant, to carry it, care for it, and camp around it.

events.title: The Arrangement of the Camp
events.description: The tribes are assigned positions around the tent of meeting by standard and ancestral house — Judah east, Reuben south, Ephraim west, Dan north — and the order of march is set.

events.title: The Census of the Levites
events.description: The Levites are counted from a month old and upward and taken by the LORD in place of the firstborn of Israel, with the surplus firstborn redeemed at five shekels each.

events.title: The Duties of the Levitical Clans
events.description: The Kohathites, Gershonites, and Merarites are counted from thirty to fifty years old and assigned their loads for carrying the sanctuary and its furnishings.

events.title: Purity of the Camp and Restitution
events.description: The unclean are put outside the camp, and those who wrong a neighbor must confess and make full restitution with a fifth added.

events.title: The Ordeal for a Suspected Wife
events.description: The ritual of the water of bitterness, by which a husband's suspicion of his wife is brought before the priest for decision.

events.title: The Nazirite Vow
events.description: Those who separate themselves to the LORD abstain from wine, leave the hair uncut, and avoid contact with the dead, with offerings prescribed for completing or interrupting the vow.

events.title: The Priestly Blessing
events.description: Aaron and his sons are given the words with which to bless Israel, invoking the LORD's blessing and keeping, the shining of his face, and the gift of peace.

events.title: The Cloud Over the Tabernacle
events.description: A cloud covers the tabernacle by day and the appearance of fire by night; Israel sets out or remains in camp only as the cloud lifts or settles.

events.title: The Two Silver Trumpets
events.description: Moses makes two trumpets of hammered silver for summoning the congregation, breaking camp, sounding the alarm in war, and marking festivals.

events.title: Israel Departs from Sinai
events.description: On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year the cloud lifts from the tabernacle and Israel sets out from the wilderness of Sinai toward the wilderness of Paran, tribe by tribe.

events.title: Fire at Taberah
events.description: The people complain in the hearing of the LORD, fire burns among them and consumes the outskirts of the camp, and the place is named Taberah.

events.title: Craving for Meat and the Complaint of Moses
events.description: The rabble crave meat and remember the fish of Egypt, weary of the manna; Moses protests to the LORD that he cannot carry this people alone.

events.title: The Seventy Elders Receive the Spirit
events.description: The LORD takes some of the spirit on Moses and puts it on seventy elders, who prophesy. Eldad and Medad prophesy in the camp, and Moses wishes that all the LORD's people were prophets.

events.title: The Quail and the Plague at Kibroth-hattaavah
events.description: A wind brings quail from the sea in vast quantity; while the meat is still between their teeth the LORD strikes the people with a great plague, and the place is called Kibroth-hattaavah, the graves of craving.

events.title: Miriam and Aaron Speak Against Moses
events.description: Miriam and Aaron object to Moses' Cushite wife and to his unique standing. The LORD vindicates Moses; Miriam becomes leprous and is shut outside the camp for seven days at Hazeroth.

events.title: Twelve Spies Sent into Canaan
events.description: One leader from each tribe is sent from the wilderness of Paran to scout Canaan. They go up through the Negeb to Hebron and cut a branch with a single cluster of grapes at the Wadi Eshcol, returning after forty days.

events.title: The Report of the Spies
events.description: The scouts report a land flowing with milk and honey but fortified cities and the descendants of Anak. Caleb urges going up at once, while the others spread a bad report of the land.

events.title: The People Refuse to Enter the Land
events.description: The congregation weeps and demands a captain to return to Egypt. Joshua and Caleb tear their clothes and plead with the people, who threaten to stone them.

events.title: Forty Years in the Wilderness Decreed
events.description: Moses intercedes and the LORD pardons, but decrees that no one counted in the census over twenty years old will enter the land except Caleb and Joshua; Israel will wander forty years, a year for each day the scouts spent in the land.

events.title: Defeat at Hormah
events.description: Presuming to go up without Moses or the ark, the people are beaten down by the Amalekites and Canaanites as far as Hormah.

events.title: Laws of Offerings in the Land
events.description: Grain and drink offerings to accompany sacrifices when Israel enters the land, provision for unintentional sin by the congregation or an individual, and the penalty for sinning high-handedly.

events.title: The Sabbath-Breaker Stoned
events.description: A man found gathering sticks on the sabbath is held in custody until the LORD's decision, then stoned outside the camp.

events.title: Fringes on the Garments
events.description: Israel is commanded to make fringes with a blue cord on the corners of their garments, to look at and remember all the commandments of the LORD.

events.title: The Rebellion of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram
events.description: Korah with 250 leaders challenges the authority of Moses and Aaron. The earth opens and swallows Dathan and Abiram with their households, and fire consumes the 250 men offering incense.

events.title: The Plague Stopped by Aaron's Censer
events.description: The censers of the dead are hammered into a covering for the altar. When the congregation blames Moses and a plague breaks out, Aaron runs among the people with incense and stands between the dead and the living.

events.title: Aaron's Rod Buds
events.description: A rod for each ancestral house is placed in the tent of meeting; Aaron's rod for the house of Levi sprouts, buds, blossoms, and bears almonds, confirming his priesthood.

events.title: The Dues of Priests and Levites
events.description: Aaron's house bears responsibility for the sanctuary. The priests receive the offerings, the Levites receive the tithe as their inheritance in place of land, and the Levites tithe in turn.

events.title: The Red Heifer and Corpse Impurity
events.description: A red heifer without defect is burned outside the camp and its ashes kept for the water for cleansing, which purifies anyone who has touched a corpse.

events.title: The Death of Miriam at Kadesh
events.description: In the first month the congregation comes into the wilderness of Zin and stays at Kadesh, where Miriam dies and is buried.

events.title: Moses Strikes the Rock at Meribah
events.description: With no water, the people quarrel with Moses. Told to command the rock, Moses strikes it twice; water comes out, but the LORD tells Moses and Aaron they will not bring the assembly into the land.

events.title: Edom Refuses Israel Passage
events.description: Moses sends messengers to the king of Edom asking to pass along the King's Highway. Edom comes out with a heavy force, and Israel turns away.

events.title: The Death of Aaron on Mount Hor
events.description: At Mount Hor, Aaron's vestments are stripped from him and put on his son Eleazar. Aaron dies on the mountain top, and Israel mourns him thirty days.

events.title: Victory Over the King of Arad
events.description: The Canaanite king of Arad takes some Israelites captive. Israel vows to devote their towns to destruction, the LORD gives them victory, and the place is named Hormah.

events.title: The Bronze Serpent
events.description: The people speak against God and Moses on the way around Edom; poisonous serpents bite them, and Moses makes a serpent of bronze on a pole so that those who look at it live.

events.title: Through Moab and the Song of the Well
events.description: Israel journeys by Oboth, Iye-abarim, and the Wadi Zered to the wilderness east of Moab, singing at Beer the song of the well that the leaders dug.

events.title: The Defeat of Sihon King of the Amorites
events.description: Sihon refuses passage and attacks Israel at Jahaz. Israel defeats him and takes possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, settling in Heshbon and its villages.

events.title: The Defeat of Og King of Bashan
events.description: Israel turns north toward Bashan; Og comes out against them at Edrei and is struck down with his sons and all his people, and Israel takes possession of his land.

events.title: Balak Summons Balaam
events.description: Camped on the plains of Moab across the Jordan from Jericho, Israel alarms Balak son of Zippor, who sends elders of Moab and Midian with fees for divination to bring Balaam son of Beor to curse Israel.

events.title: Balaam's Donkey and the Angel
events.description: As Balaam rides to Moab, his donkey sees the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword and turns aside three times. The LORD opens the donkey's mouth, and then Balaam's eyes.

events.title: Balaam's First and Second Oracles
events.description: At Bamoth-baal and the field of Zophim, seven altars are built and bulls and rams offered. Twice Balaam blesses Israel instead of cursing them, to Balak's fury.

events.title: Balaam's Final Oracles
events.description: The spirit of God comes upon Balaam and he blesses Israel a third time, praising the beauty of their tents and encampments, then prophesies a star coming out of Jacob before returning home.

events.title: Apostasy at Baal-Peor and the Zeal of Phinehas
events.description: Israel joins itself to the Baal of Peor through the women of Moab. A plague kills twenty-four thousand and is stopped when Phinehas son of Eleazar spears an Israelite man and a Midianite woman.

events.title: The Second Census on the Plains of Moab
events.description: After the plague, a new census counts 601,730 men of war. Not one remains of those counted at Sinai except Caleb and Joshua, and the land is to be apportioned by lot according to these numbers.

events.title: The Daughters of Zelophehad
events.description: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah ask for their father's inheritance since he left no son. The LORD grants their request and establishes it as a statute of judgment for Israel.

events.title: Joshua Commissioned to Succeed Moses
events.description: Moses is told to view the land from the mountains of Abarim, since he will not enter it. He lays his hands on Joshua son of Nun before Eleazar and the congregation, giving him some of his authority.

events.title: The Calendar of Public Offerings
events.description: The daily, sabbath, new moon, and festival offerings are set out in full for passover, weeks, trumpets, the day of atonement, and the seven days of booths.

events.title: Laws Concerning Vows
events.description: A man who makes a vow must keep it; the vows of a daughter or wife stand unless annulled by her father or husband on the day he hears of it.

events.title: The War Against Midian
events.description: A thousand from each tribe go out against Midian and kill its five kings and Balaam son of Beor. The spoil is divided between the warriors and the congregation, with a levy for the LORD.

events.title: Reuben, Gad, and Half of Manasseh Settle in Transjordan
events.description: Seeing good grazing land at Jazer and Gilead, Reuben and Gad ask to settle east of the Jordan. Moses agrees on condition that their fighting men cross over armed until Israel takes possession of Canaan.

events.title: The Record of the Wilderness Journey
events.description: Moses writes down the stages of the journey from Rameses, set out on the fifteenth day of the first month, through forty-two encampments to the plains of Moab by the Jordan.

events.title: The Boundaries of Canaan and the Tribal Leaders
events.description: Israel is commanded to drive out the inhabitants and destroy their idols. The borders of the land are drawn, and Eleazar, Joshua, and one leader from each tribe are named to apportion it.

events.title: Levitical Cities and Cities of Refuge
events.description: Forty-eight towns with pasture lands are assigned to the Levites, six of them cities of refuge where one who kills without intent may flee from the avenger of blood until the death of the high priest.

events.title: The Marriage of Zelophehad's Daughters
events.description: So that no inheritance passes from tribe to tribe, heiresses must marry within their father's tribe; Zelophehad's daughters marry sons of their father's brothers in Manasseh.
